items.title: Compact objects in the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category are summands of finite complexes built from generators
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma describes compact objects of D(A) for a Grothendieck abelian category with a generating set S satisfying two conditions: every compact object is a direct summand of a finite complex of finite direct sums of elements of S (statement lines 13933-13946). The proof has three substantial parts: compactness is used twice to replace infinite constructions by finite ones, first to make K bounded below through the canonical truncations (proof lines 13949-13961) and then to factor the identity through a bounded complex L with terms in direct sums of S (proof lines 13967-13989); the technical heart is the improvement claim, where assumption (2) on the functor Hom_A(E, -) and compactness of K cut a direct sum L^c down to a finite subsum through which the differential factors and whose remaining projection becomes zero after composing with varphi (proof lines 14001-14017); finally the kernel of that projection gives a distinguished triangle from which a new factorisation is extracted using the homological behaviour of Hom_{D(A)}(K, -) (proof lines 14018-14031), and the idempotent so obtained is split to display K as a direct summand (proof lines 13990-13998). The claim is H2: a long but completely written-out argument whose only inputs are the two displayed assumptions and standard results of the derived-category chapters.
